newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strikes, fires hit Gold Fields Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: Strikes, fires hit Gold Fields Q3 profit.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd reported a sharp drop in third quarter profits on Monday, dragged down by strikes and fires at its largest mines.
Combined net profits before capital expenditure for its three gold mining companies was down to 274.41 million rand from 355.86 in the preceding quarter.
The company said production and revenue were hard hit by fires and a spate of violent industrial action.
"The group results have been characterised by violent conflict at two of the operations and fires in another two of the operations.

"This has resulted in less tonnes milled for the quarter at lower grades and unfortunately, obviously lower revenue for the quarter," said Keith Spencer, Gold Fields general manager of gold operations.

Total gold production for Deelkraal Gold Mining Co Ltd, Driefontein Consolidated Ltd and Kloof Gold Mining Co Ltd was 21,172 kg versus 23,021 kg on a milling rate of 2,643,000 tonnes versus 2,630,000 tonnes.
Yields averaged 8.0 grams per tonne against 8.4 g/t in the three months to end-June.
The average working cost was 43,097 rand per kg versus 37,370 and the average gold price received was 55,164 rand a kg versus 53,629.
Driefontein's production was worst hit by fires and labour violence.

Net profit before capex was 177.47 million rand against the 225.60 million rand in the June quarter. Capital expenditure at the mine's East Driefontein and West Driefontein divisions was 121.56 million rand.
Gold output at East Dries dropped to 4,839 kg from 5,459.5 kg in the June quarter and at West Dries output in the September quarter was 5,386.1 kg versus the 5,840 kg in the previous quarter.
Production at the Kloof gold mine was also affected by an underground fire at the Kloof division and violent ethnic clashes at the mine's Leeudoorn division.
At Deelkraal, gold production dropped to 1,718 kg from 1,844 kg in the previous quarter, mainly due to lower stope values.
But Gold Fields said it expected improved tonnage milled and average yields at all its mines in the December quarter.
Working costs for the three gold mining companies increased by six percent to 912 million rand from 860.3 million in the previous quarter.
Unit working costs increased by 15 percent to 43,097 rand per kg of gold produced from the 37,370 in the previous quarter.
Gold Fields said the increase reflected in part the higher wages negotiated between the Chamber of Mines employer body and the National Union of Mineworkers.
